subject: Azure Marketplace: publisher identity verification & offer JSON sanity pass
messages:
From: Samuel Liu <samuel.liu@contoso.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Azure Marketplace Support <azure-marketplace@microsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Publisher setup + initial questions for listing Redwood-enabled offering

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the intro last week. We're ready to start the Azure Marketplace listing for the Redwood-managed deployment of our analytics SaaS. A couple of quick questions before we begin the offer package:

- Do we register as an individual publisher (Contoso) and add Redwood as co-publisher, or should Redwood register the publisher account and we grant access?
- What exact artifacts do you need from us for the initial offer JSON and ARM manifest?
- Is SOC2 evidence required to pass technical validation, or can we provide a SOC2-in-progress note?

We want to avoid repeated resubmissions. If you can send a concise checklist and example offer payload, that would speed things up. Also please advise on typical timelines for the Azure validation gate.

Thanks,
Samuel Liu
Marketplace Program Manager
Contoso Corp
Attachments: none

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Publisher setup + initial questions for listing Redwood-enabled offering

Folks — forwarding Contoso's note. Quick coordination: can you confirm who will own which artifacts and whether we have an updated checklist to hand off? I started an internal checklist (attached). Key items we must confirm with Contoso:

- Publisher account flow: We generally ask the customer (Contoso) to own the publisher account and add Redwood as co-publisher or publishing agent. This avoids MPN/ownership issues. We can sign the co-publisher paperwork.
- Required artifacts: offer manifest (offer ID/plan SKUs), offer listing images, privacy & compliance statements, ARM template or SaaS offer redirect URIs, SSO metadata (if applicable), support contact, MPN ID, tenant ID for subscription mapping, and signed attestation.
- SOC2: Azure will accept "SOC2 in progress" in some cases but it slows co-sell enablement. Recommend customer provide whatever audit evidence they have and a date for SOC2 completion.

Marissa — take lead on legal/attestation and assets. Karthik — take the offer JSON/ARM template and validate SKU naming + plan redirects. I expect Azure technical validation to be ~3-5 business days once the package is correct; common delays come from manifest mismatches and bad redirect URIs.

Attaching: azure_publisher_checklist.xlsx (internal template).

Thanks,
Priya
Head of GTM Partnerships (Platform Partnerships)
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Publisher setup + initial questions for listing Redwood-enabled offering

Agree with the split. Short checklist summary for internal handoff (I will send this to Contoso with the items they need to fill):

1) Publisher identity: Confirm MPN ID and legal publisher name (must match MPN).
2) Contact list: support email, legal contact, sales contact.
3) Offer package: offer_sample.json (manifest), listing images (1024x512 + 128x128), description markdown, pricing plan descriptions.
4) Technical artifacts: ARM manifest (if deploying resources), SaaS offer redirect URI(s) and token exchange spec, example provisioning webhook.
5) Security/compliance: SOC2 report or letter + data handling summary + support for customer data residency (if required).
6) Legal: signed attestation (I'll prepare DocuSign).

Gotchas: offerId must be lowercase ASCII, SKU names cannot contain spaces or special chars, image names should not exceed 64 chars. Azure often rejects manifests for missing planDisplayName fields.

I'll create the DocuSign for the attestation and attach the sample offer JSON. Karthik — once you confirm the ARM example, I'll send the full list to Contoso.

Marissa
Sr. Partner Ops
Redwood Inference

Timeline: once we receive a complete package, Azure validation typically takes 3 business days. If we need to iterate on the manifest, allow an additional 2-4 days. For co-sell enablement with Microsoft field teams, opt-in can take 1-2 weeks after validation.
